situation: In September 2012, water released from the Lagdo dam and heavy rains flooded villages along the Benue near Garoua. Farmers lost their fields and houses.
Six months later, in March, the same farmers waited for rain under a burning sun to plant their millet. Hamza wonders how the same area can suffer from too much water and from too little water.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that the same area suffers from floods in the rainy season and from lack of water in the dry season.
What caused the floods of September 2012?
They were caused by heavy rains and by water released from the Lagdo dam.
What can farmers do to reduce these problems?
They can avoid building on the floodplain, store water for the dry season and plant trees.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand floods, droughts and desertification, which are major hazards in North Cameroon.

qa.q: Look at the map. Which areas of North Cameroon are often flooded, and which are threatened by drought and desertification?
qa.a: The floodplains of the Benue (Garoua) and of the Logone (Yagoua, Kousseri) are often flooded. The Far North is threatened by drought and desertification.

qa.q: What is the difference between a drought and desertification?
qa.a: A drought is a temporary period with too little rain. Desertification is a lasting change: fertile land becomes desert.

sum.title: I. Meaning and Areas of Occurrence
defs: A flood is the covering of normally dry land by water.
A drought is a long period of abnormally low rainfall that causes a shortage of water.
Desertification is the degradation of land in dry areas, which slowly turns into desert.
items: Areas of Occurrence
Floods occur on floodplains, such as the Benue near Garoua and the Logone near Yagoua and Kousseri. Droughts and desertification affect the Sahel and the Far North Region.
cmr_hazards.png

qa.q: Give two causes of floods along the Benue.
qa.a: Heavy, long rains that rivers cannot contain, and the sudden release of water from the Lagdo dam. Deforestation also increases runoff.

qa.q: Give two human causes of desertification in the Far North.
qa.a: Cutting trees for firewood and charcoal, overgrazing and poor farming methods leave the soil bare and exhausted.

sum.title: II. Causes
items: A. Causes of Floods
– Heavy and prolonged rainfall.
– Release of water from dams or dam failure.
– Deforestation, which increases runoff.
– Building on floodplains and blocked drains.
B. Causes of Droughts and Desertification
– Low and irregular rainfall, made worse by global warming.
– Cutting trees for firewood and charcoal.
– Overgrazing and bush fires.
– Poor farming methods that exhaust the soil.

qa.q: Give two effects of floods and two effects of drought on people.
qa.a: Floods destroy houses, crops and roads, and spread cholera. Droughts cause crop failure, famine, loss of livestock and migration.

sum.title: III. Effects
items: A. Effects of Floods
Floods destroy houses, roads, bridges and crops, drown people and animals, and spread waterborne diseases such as cholera.
B. Effects of Droughts and Desertification
They cause crop failure, famine, death of livestock, migration to towns and conflicts over water and pasture.

qa.q: How can people protect themselves from floods?
qa.a: By building dykes, controlling the release of water from dams, warning people in time, and not building on floodplains.

qa.q: How can people fight desertification in the Far North?
qa.a: By planting trees (Opération Sahel Vert, Great Green Wall), using improved stoves, controlling grazing and storing water.

sum.title: IV. Adaptations and Mitigations
items: A. Against Floods
Build dykes and drains, control dam releases, set up early warning systems, avoid building on floodplains and replant forests.
B. Against Droughts and Desertification
Plant trees (Opération Sahel Vert, Great Green Wall), grow drought-resistant crops, store water, control grazing and use improved stoves.

evaluation: Where do floods often occur in North Cameroon?
Floods often occur on the floodplains of the Benue near Garoua and of the Logone near Yagoua and Kousseri.
Give two human causes of desertification.
Two human causes are cutting trees for firewood and overgrazing.
Flood water mixes with sewage and pollutes drinking water.
remediation: The covering of dry land by water is a ______.
A long period of low rainfall is a ______.
The degradation of dry land into desert is ______.
Too many animals grazing on the same land is ______.
The dam whose releases can flood the Benue valley is ______.
The African tree-planting project across the Sahel is the Great Green ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. flood 2. drought 3. desertification 4. overgrazing 5. Lagdo 6. Wall
